children: shares surrendered early gains and slipped into the red as investors reconsidered the company’s most recent quarterly results, which reflected flat profit margins and a weaker liquidity position, overshadowing otherwise upbeat results.
The stock failed to breach the 50- and 100-day moving averages at the open, driving CHWY as much as 9% lower for a fourth straight session of declines.

“Results were not as good as they looked,” argues Jefferies analyst Kaumil Gajrawala, as the revenue beat was fueled by one-time items including tariff refunds, rebate timing, and gift card breakage. This was reflected in the company’s profit margin, which was roughly unchanged from a year ago. Looking ahead to the current quarter, Chewy
expects to see gross margin decline modestly on a sequential basis, consistent with the seasonality experienced last year.

raised its full-year targets, management warned that pet spending will likely remain flat for the rest of the year as the pet market remains "strained" and higher fuel costs will continue to be a headwind on profitability for the rest of the year.
During the earnings call, management also noted the challenged pricing environment that is unlikely to "meaningfully" recover in the second half of the year.

“What that means is we don’t expect pricing to be a net benefit in 2026,” Chewy CEO Sumit Singh said on the call, while CFO Chris Deppe added that the guidance does not assume any recovery or improvement in consumer behavior.

title: Chewy reverses early gains as margin, liquidity concerns weigh
